idea: A pre-order page for a café's morning pastries.

decision: Pay online when ordering, or pay at pickup
options: Pay online at order
Pay at pickup
Pay online, with pay-at-pickup for regulars
recommendation: Pay online at order
reason: Paying upfront commits the customer so the café can bake the right amount and avoid unsold or no-show pastries, and it is the simplest end-to-end version.

decision: What happens to the money if someone cancels or doesn't collect
options: Full refund until a cutoff time (e.g. night before), none after
No refunds, but offer credit for another day
Always refund in full
recommendation: Full refund until a cutoff time (e.g. night before), none after
reason: Pastries are baked to order, so a clear cutoff protects the café from waste while still feeling fair to the customer.

decision: How prices are shown and set for pre-orders
options: Same price as in-café, shown per item
Small pre-order discount or bundle (e.g. box of 6)
Add a pre-order fee
recommendation: Same price as in-café, shown per item
reason: Matching shelf prices is the smallest version that works, and discounts or bundles can wait for evidence of demand.

note: Pricing and payment choices for a café morning-pastry pre-order page: when customers pay, cancellation promise, and how prices are shown.

decision: The one number that says the page worked
options: Count pre-orders placed per morning
Count page visits per morning
Total pre-order revenue per week
recommendation: Count pre-orders placed per morning
reason: Orders placed is the smallest number that shows customers actually used the page, and it needs no extra tracking.

decision: What to keep about each customer who orders
options: Name and phone number only until pickup, then delete
Name, phone and email kept indefinitely
No contact details, just an order number
recommendation: Name and phone number only until pickup, then delete
reason: We only need a way to identify the customer at pickup, and collected personal data can't be un-collected later.

decision: How to tell that a pre-order was actually picked up
options: Count orders marked collected by staff at pickup
Count orders never collected (no-shows)
Do not track pickup
recommendation: Count orders marked collected by staff at pickup
reason: Collected versus placed shows whether pre-ordering produces real sales or wasted pastries, which decides if the page is worth keeping.

note: Data view of the pre-order page: one success number for the whole page, plus what to keep from order placement and pickup, since her journey has no boxes yet.

decision: Whether to cap pre-orders per pastry or per pickup slot
options: Cap per pastry by daily bake quantity
Cap per pickup slot
No cap, café handles overflow
recommendation: Cap per pastry by daily bake quantity
reason: We'd first learn how many of each pastry the café bakes and sells out of, because promising a pastry that's gone is the worst failure for a pre-order.

decision: Whether customers pay online when ordering or pay at pickup
options: Pay at pickup
Pay online at checkout
recommendation: Pay at pickup
reason: We'd learn first whether customers expect to pay ahead; pay-at-pickup is the smallest version that works end to end and avoids handling money and refunds.

decision: How customers choose a pickup time and the order cut-off
options: Fixed 15-minute pickup slots with a evening-before cut-off
Free-text pickup time
Just 'morning', no time chosen
recommendation: Fixed 15-minute pickup slots with a evening-before cut-off
reason: We'd learn first when customers actually come in and when the café needs notice to bake, and named slots in plain words like 'Pick up at 8:15' let both sides plan.

note: Listed the three main open decisions for the café pre-order page, all framed as what we'd learn first, since the one finding (group-class waitlists) doesn't apply to a pastry pre-order.

decision: What a sold-out or cut-off pastry shows on the menu
options: Keep it listed, greyed, with a plain 'Sold out for tomorrow' line and no button
Hide it from the list
Keep it listed with a 'Tell me when back' button
recommendation: Keep it listed, greyed, with a plain 'Sold out for tomorrow' line and no button
reason: Customers see the full menu and trust the stock; one filled button stays reserved for the main action, and the smallest version needs no waitlist (L2).

decision: What leads the page: pickup time or the pastry list
options: Pickup day and time picker first, then pastries
Pastry list first, pickup time at checkout
Both on one screen with a sticky summary bar
recommendation: Pastry list first, pickup time at checkout
reason: Customers think 'what can I get' before 'when', and putting items first is how they would say it (L1); hierarchy leads with the thing named by headings, not a form.

decision: Which single accent colour the page uses, and where
options: Warm crust orange on the one filled button and the order count only
Deep berry red used on prices and buttons
No accent, ink and paper only
recommendation: Warm crust orange on the one filled button and the order count only
reason: Interface stays 90 to 95% neutral with one accent per surface, and the accent marks the main action; it must avoid violet hues and keep 7:1 text contrast on ink.

note: Sketched the pre-order page structure: what leads the menu, how sold-out pastries show, and the single accent.

decision: What happens when a pastry sells out or the day's batch is full
options: Show live remaining count and mark items 'Sold out' when gone
Accept orders without limits and let the café sort it out
Cap total orders per pickup slot only
recommendation: Show live remaining count and mark items 'Sold out' when gone
reason: Pastries are baked in limited batches, so promising something that isn't there breaks customer trust and costs the café a refund.

decision: How customers choose pickup time and when ordering closes
options: Pick a pickup window; ordering closes the evening before
Pick a pickup window; ordering closes a set time before that window
No time choice, everything ready at opening
recommendation: Pick a pickup window; ordering closes the evening before
reason: The café needs to know the night before what to bake, and customers want a time that fits their commute.

decision: Whether customers pay online or at pickup
options: Pay at pickup, no online payment in v1
Pay online when ordering
Pay online only for large orders
recommendation: Pay at pickup, no online payment in v1
reason: It is the smallest version that works end to end, though no-shows become the café's risk and we should watch for them.

note: Drafted the key journey decisions for the café morning-pastry pre-order page: sell-out handling, pickup timing and cutoff, and payment.

decision: What happens when someone orders the last pastry another person just took
options: Hold stock per order for a few minutes, then release it
Check stock at submit and show 'just sold out' with alternatives
Accept all orders and let the café sort out shortages
recommendation: Check stock at submit and show 'just sold out' with alternatives
reason: A single atomic stock check at submit is the plain, proven way to avoid overselling, and it needs no timers or held-stock logic.

decision: Whether pickup time slots have a cap on orders
options: Fixed number of orders per 15-minute slot, then slot shows full
No slots, just a 'ready by' morning window
Slots with no cap, only a cutoff time
recommendation: Fixed number of orders per 15-minute slot, then slot shows full
reason: A cap keeps the counter from being swamped at rush time and is simple to count and enforce.

decision: How the customer gets their order confirmation
options: Email only, sent right after order
Text message only
On-screen confirmation plus email
recommendation: On-screen confirmation plus email
reason: The on-screen confirmation works even if delivery fails, and email is the cheapest reliable channel with no phone field needed.
